div.head: Records
div.p: A record is a thing the texts are about, or come from, which the application keeps once and every file points to: a person, a place, an institution, an event, a manuscript, a publication, a work and its versions. A file names records where its text names them (), and may list them, with what it knows of them, in its standOff: persons in listPerson, places in listPlace, institutions in listOrg, events in listEvent, works, versions and publications in listBibl. Every record may have its names, its dates in the one form (), its ids elsewhere, its sources, notes, and its relations to other records (). Manuscripts have a part of their own (), and publications will ().
Persons are common, since most files list those they name; the rest is full.

div.head: Placeholders, ids and permalinks
div.p: A record listed in a file has an xml:id, which the file's names point to by ref (#new_person_Arno):

list.item: a record's, for one it has: its kind and its number (PERS.1234); a work's or a version's is its code (C.NIC-0325).

div.p: A name may also point to a record the file doesn't list, by its permalink (https://…/id/person/PERS.1234), which the import uses as given. An export points by permalinks, and lists the records it points to, with their names, so that the file reads on its own (). The records of the Council of Carthage of 397 list its two councils by placeholders, with their dates:

div.head: Persons
div.p: A person is a person, with one main name, persName typed main, and any number typed alternative: the spellings and forms the sources use. A person's life is dated by birth, death and floruit, in the one form. Simplician of Milan, in the records of the Council of Carthage of 397, revised to the one form: born about 320, died in 400 or 401:
A person in the standOff has a record's id or a placeholder's; a placeholder's person has one main name; a floruit gives its dates. Each is checked:
Offices and roles, a scribe's hand, an author's works, are relations from the person (), not parts of the record.

constraintSpec.desc: A person listed in the standOff is a record or a placeholder for one.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A person in the standOff has an @xml:id: a record's (PERS. and a number, or solemne_person_ and a number), or a placeholder's (new_person_ and a name).

constraintSpec.desc: A new person has one main name.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A new person has one main name (persName typed main).
A floruit gives its dates in its attributes.

div.head: Places
div.p: A place is a place, with its name, placeName, and, where known, its location: the country, region and settlement it lies in, and its coordinates in geo (latitude, then longitude). Benediktbeuern, which owned a manuscript in Munich, as Mirabile gives it:
A diocese, a province, a kingdom: each a place, its kind in type ().

div.head: Institutions
div.p: An institution, a religious house, a chapter, a library, is an org, its kind in type, with one main name, orgName typed main. Where it stands is a relation to a place, as an owner's is (). A name of an institution elsewhere in the file points to its record by ref, as other names do. The abbey of Benediktbeuern, with its id in Mirabile:

org.orgName: SS. Benedikt und Jakob, abbazia OSB

div.head: Events
div.p: An event, a council or a synod, is an event, dated in its attributes in the one form. TEI 4.12 lets it hold a name (eventName), or a description, or paragraphs, not two of them; a name is what the import reads first. Where it took place, and what it enacted, are relations (). An event points to a record by ref, or describes one, and its description has words:

constraintSpec.desc: An event points to a record, or describes one.

sch:rule.sch:assert: An event points to a record (@ref) or describes one, with eventName or p.

div.head: Works and versions
div.p: A work, a council's canons or a collection, and each of its versions, a translation or a recension, is a bibl in listBibl, typed work or version (). It holds its title, its author by ref, its code (an untyped idno), its category (an idno typed category), and its date in the one form. A version is a version of its work by a relation (). Mirabile's Institutiones of Justinian, from a manuscript's records, revised to the form of a work:

A work names its canonical version, whose canons are the work's, and, where that version has no text in the application, the version whose text stands in for it; otherwise the earliest version with a text stands in. Both are defaults the project chooses, not claims about the texts, so they are pointers in the work's record, ptr typed canonical and stand-in, to the versions' records. Nicaea's canons are canonical in Greek, which the corpus doesn't hold; a made-up record lets a Latin version stand in:

bibl.title: Council of Nicaea, 325, the Greek canons
Council of Nicaea, 325, in Dionysius Exiguus's translation

div.p: A pointer of another type is an error:
The import makes a provisional work or version of a placeholder, and reads its canonical and stand-in choices; an export writes each work and version it points to, with them.

valItem.desc: in a work's record: its canonical version
in a work's record: the version whose text stands in for the canonical version's
in a relation's description: the work, version or transcription a text came through

div.head: Witnesses
div.p: A witness is a copy of a text: in a manuscript, at its folios, or in a publication, at its pages (). A file names the witnesses it needs in the source description's listWit, each a witness with an xml:id, holding a pointer to its manuscript or publication and its folios or pages: an edition carrying the page breaks of several manuscripts points to each from its page breaks by edRef (), and a reconstruction lists the witnesses its editor reconstructed it from (). A made-up list:
The import joins each witness to its manuscript or publication, at its folios or pages.

div.head: Work groups
div.p: A work group is a scholarly construct over several works, "the Pseudo-Isidorian forgeries": a listBibl typed workGroup, with its name in head, what it is in desc, and its members, each a bibl holding a ptr to the work's record (TEI lets a list of bibliography hold only bibliographic items). Every heading is typed (); a group's name is typed rubric, which says nothing more there. A made-up group:

listBibl.head: The Pseudo-Isidorian forgeries
listBibl.desc: The forgeries made in the circle of the False Decretals, in the middle of the 9th century.

div.p: A group is stored with its name, description, author and members; it is never a level of a text.

div.head: Rare kinds and extra fields
div.p: A record of a kind the guide has no section for, a diocese or a religious order, takes the nearest form, with its kind in type: a diocese is a place, an order an org. A name of it in the text is an rs, its kind in type and its record in ref (). The kinds and their fields are defined in the application, as in Heurist; a field the form has no element for is an f, named as the field, in an fs typed by the kind, in a note typed extra: TEI lets a place, an institution or an event hold an fs only in a note, and every kind does the same. A made-up diocese:
Only a kind that no form fits needs a new section of the guide.

div.head: Ids elsewhere
div.p: A record's ids in other projects' catalogues are idnos, each typed by its authority, from a closed list: wikidata, viaf, gnd, geonames, tgn, pleiades, mirabile, clavis, biblissima, schoenberg, hmml, bodleian, manusOnline, and the Bodleian's ieArk, crArk and SCN (). The import keeps them beside the record's own id, and matches by them. Justinian, as Mirabile names him, with his id there:

The project's earlier files give these links as a note typed links holding a list of links, or typed authorities; the import reads an authority's link as its id. Such a note holds only its list, and each link its target and words:

constraintSpec.desc: A note of links holds a list of links.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A note of links holds a list of links, and no words of its own.

constraintSpec.desc: A link has a target and words.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A link has a @target and words.

div.head: Sources
div.p: Every record, text and annotation names where it comes from. A record's source is a bibl typed source in it: the source's name, the record's id there (an idno typed by the authority), a link to it (ref), the date it was taken (date typed retrieved), and the licence it was taken under (licence, in availability). The import keeps it as the record's provenance. The Institutiones again, with its source:
